parts.text: What does the heating evidence support?

options.text: Sugar is a compound because heating breaks it into different substances.
Sugar is an element because it was a single white solid before heating.
Sugar is an element because any black solid left after heating must be an element.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Anika heats a little sugar strongly. It chars, gives off vapours, and leaves a black solid. She is told that this shows sugar is not a single element.

part_answers.answer: An element cannot be broken into different substances by heating; sugar can, so sugar is a compound.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating sugar yields new substances, so sugar is a compound, not an element. A white solid look or a black residue alone does not make it an element.
